title: Choose Utu's home composition
question: The visual world is fixed. Choose the operating model to carry into the Rust/Leptos build.

options.label: Attention-led split
options.thesis: Everything needing a decision leads; current work stays visible beside it.
options.viewport: A 62/38 split gives owner decisions the larger field and live agents the narrower field, with fleet truth along the bottom.
options.risk: Projects become context inside rows rather than the primary spatial model.

options.label: Project-led workbench
options.lineage: project index, task table, and inspector
options.thesis: The selected project holds tasks, agents, sessions, evidence, and owner controls in one stable workspace.
options.viewport: A project list, task table, and selected-task inspector form the core, while an exception bar keeps attention visible.
options.risk: The home view feels more like managing one project than surveying the whole fleet.

options.label: Fleet-led activity
options.lineage: fleet index, evidence timeline, and decision rail
options.thesis: A live evidence stream makes agents, handoffs, tool use, inference, cost, and owner decisions observable together.
options.viewport: Fleet state anchors the left, a live session timeline owns the center, and three owner decisions remain sticky on the right.
options.risk: Continuous events can dominate the quieter project and task-management workflows.
